headline: High: ECC can write shared files and use MCP while RD-Agent uploads data to third-party APIs, creating default-path leakage and conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write filesystem and use MCP, and RD-Agent reads/writes logs and runs browsers. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from one agent influence the other, but no direct shared channel is documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or log directory
IF one agent ingests the other's file output as instructions without sanitization
mitigations: Separate workspaces and log directories
Disable MCP routes that accept untrusted file content
Add a manual review step before copying outputs between agents
Use read-only mounts for shared reference data

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, hooks, git history, and MCP configs; RD-Agent handles financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, and logs while calling OpenAI/Azure/DeepSeek/Kaggle APIs. If they share data or credentials, sensitive material can flow into third-party inference or logs. The pairwise path is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF both agents access the same sensitive dataset or report files
IF either agent forwards those files into its listed external APIs
mitigations: Keep sensitive datasets out of shared folders
Rotate and scope API keys to the minimum needed
Disable logging of prompts and file contents where possible
Review outbound API destinations before execution

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has unrestricted filesystem write, modify_git_state, and network egress; RD-Agent has broad network egress and browser access. Both support multiple instances, so concurrent writes or API-driven side effects can collide. Because ECC explicitly writes git state and RD-Agent writes logs, the overlap is dangerous by default when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or output directory
IF both are allowed to mutate git state or shared logs concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate repositories or output roots
Serialize write access with a lock file
Run one agent read-only during the other's write phase
Snapshot the workspace before concurrent runs

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC produces session summaries, security findings, and documentation; RD-Agent is a research automation agent that can act on papers, datasets, and logs. If RD-Agent consumes ECC output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream research artifacts or actions. No verification step is documented between them, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF RD-Agent uses ECC-generated summaries or findings as input
IF no independent verification step is inserted before RD-Agent acts
mitigations: Require a human review of ECC outputs before reuse
Add source citations to every transferred finding
Compare ECC outputs against original files or logs
Limit RD-Agent to drafting, not acting, on ECC outputs

E_compliance.rationale: ECC handles session data, hooks, and security findings with default local paths, while RD-Agent processes financial reports, execution traces, and logs and sends data to external model APIs. If regulated or sensitive data is shared across the pair, retention and residency policies can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so this remains a medium-risk mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data such as financial reports or security findings is routed through both agents
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the two execution environments
mitigations: Keep regulated data in a separate compliant workspace
Confirm retention settings for both agents before use
Avoid sending regulated content to external APIs
Document which agent may store which data class
